column1: # The table of tools (ADR 0015, DESIGN.md 13.2): how each known VPN or circumvention app runs on Android, so that
# Watch can find the user's tool and chain apps through it (W6) without guessing. One row per package; evidence in sources.tsv.
#   modes              vpn, proxy (runs without VpnService and serves a local proxy), or none (neither: a messenger or browser)
#   proxy-label        what the app calls proxy mode in its English UI; '(...)' describes a switch with no name of its own; '-' none
#   proxy              listeners in proxy mode with default settings, comma separated, each protocol:address:port, where protocol is
#                      socks5, http (HTTP CONNECT) or mixed (SOCKS5 and HTTP on one port); address 127.0.0.1, [::1] or 0.0.0.0;
#                      'profile' when the user's profile defines them and the app has no default; '-' no proxy mode
#   auth               SOCKS5 username and password: none (cannot be set), optional (can be set, off by default), default (on by default)
#   udp                yes, no: SOCKS5 UDP ASSOCIATE works with default settings
#   domain-names       yes, no: the SOCKS5 server takes domain names (ATYP 3), so names go to the tool
#   proxy-in-vpn       yes, no, profile: a loopback proxy also listens while the tool runs as a VPN, with default settings
#   per-app            yes, no: the tool's VPN mode can include or exclude chosen apps
#   wireguard          import, export (comma separated), provider (the provider's website issues .conf files), or no: whether the app
#                      reads or writes a standard WireGuard configuration (.conf, zip or wireguard:// link)
# In every column, 'unknown' means no primary source settles it, '-' means it does not apply, and a value ending in '?' comes from a
# source that does not settle it (a stale tree, docs for another platform, a third-party report) and needs a device test.
# 'no' for a feature means it was not found in the app's source at the commit in sources.tsv.

column13: No proxy-only mode: the app always establishes its VPN. Internal SOCKS and HTTP listeners on loopback, on ports chosen at run time, feed that VPN

A browser with its own tor, not a VPN. Its SOCKS port is a Unix socket in the app's private directory; a TCP SOCKS port opens only if the pref extensions.torlauncher.socks_port_use_tcp is set, and then on a random port

A browser with its own tor, not a VPN. Its SOCKS port is a Unix socket in the app's private directory; a TCP SOCKS port opens only if the pref extensions.torlauncher.socks_port_use_tcp is set, and then on a random port

http is Tor's HTTPTunnelPort (HTTP CONNECT only). If 9050 or 8118 is taken (InviZible uses the same ports), Orbot moves to the next free port. Tor accepts any SOCKS username and password and uses them only to isolate streams; it never asks for one. UDP ASSOCIATE is refused: Tor carries TCP only. An 'all interfaces' setting binds 0.0.0.0
Beta. Carries apps over Tor with onionmasq inside its VPN; no local SOCKS listener found in the app source (onionmasq itself not read)

No local proxy found in the app source. WireGuard .conf files come from account.protonvpn.com (Downloads, WireGuard configuration), Free plan included with fewer options; the app itself neither imports nor exports them

F-Droid build of the same source. No local proxy found in the app source. WireGuard .conf files come from account.protonvpn.com (Downloads, WireGuard configuration), Free plan included with fewer options; the app itself neither imports nor exports them
Messenger, not a VPN. It can itself use a Signal TLS proxy; it opens no local proxy
Messenger with its own Tor, not a VPN. Its tor takes SOCKS connections on port 59050 (59052 in debug builds) for Briar's own use; bind address not read

No mode switch: the app runs as a VPN only if the profile has a tun inbound, otherwise without VpnService. Listeners, ports and users all come from the profile; the app has no default port. WireGuard only as a sing-box endpoint in the profile, no .conf import

Ports are 2080 (SOCKS5) and 9080 (HTTP, off by default) plus the Android user number, so a second user or work profile gets 2081. The SOCKS inbound can be turned off and its UDP turned off. Core: exclave-core, a v2ray-core fork; its SOCKS port does not answer HTTP

Turning the VPN switch off starts ProxyService instead of VpnService. Authentication covers every inbound, and the app empties skip-auth-prefixes so loopback is not exempt. Allow LAN binds all addresses. Core: mihomo (Clash.Meta fork)

Not a tunnel: ByeDPI changes how packets look to get past DPI and sends traffic straight to the destination from the phone. Names in SOCKS requests are resolved by ByeDPI through the system resolver, so DNS goes to the network's resolver. A setting turns domain names off. Chaining through it hides nothing from the network

WireGuard and AmneziaWG client. Proxy mode runs the tunnel in user space (wireproxy-awg) without VpnService; names are resolved through the tunnel. One username and password covers both ports; SOCKS4 only without credentials

Port is 2080 plus the Android user number. The mixed inbound has no user setting, so it cannot take a password. 'Allow Connections from the LAN' binds 0.0.0.0. Last release February 2026; Google Play listing controlled by a third party (apps.tsv)

Since April 2026: optional username and password, a random-port option (10000 to 65535, off by default), and switches to turn the local proxy or its UDP off. Xray builds answer HTTP on the SOCKS port; v2fly-core builds and forks put HTTP on 10809. 'Allow connections from the LAN' drops the 127.0.0.1 bind. Exports WireGuard as a wireguard:// link

F-Droid flavour of the same source. Since April 2026: optional username and password, a random-port option (10000 to 65535, off by default), and switches to turn the local proxy or its UDP off. Xray builds answer HTTP on the SOCKS port; v2fly-core builds and forks put HTTP on 10809. 'Allow connections from the LAN' drops the 127.0.0.1 bind. Exports WireGuard as a wireguard:// link
Release builds are VPN only. The build script also makes 'stealth-novpn' builds, which ship under other package names; their proxy was not traced

Also ::1:12334 when IPv6 is on. The local port opens in VPN mode only if 'local proxy in VPN' is on. With 'local proxy auth' on, it asks for user 'hiddify' and the LAN-sharing secret. LAN sharing opens a second port, 12338, on all addresses, always with the secret. Clash API on 16756 is on by default. Licence adds non-commercial terms
The local proxy (Xray on 127.0.0.1:10808, Premium only) is built only into desktop builds; on Android isSupported() returns false, so a listener on 10808 on a phone is not Amnezia
Fork of the WireGuard app with AmneziaWG obfuscation: same file, zip and QR import and zip export

Turning 'Route System Traffic' off runs ClashService without VpnService. Ports come only from the profile or an override; the app sets none. Many subscription profiles use 7890 (mixed) or 7891 (SOCKS), a convention, not an app default. Binds 127.0.0.1 unless the profile sets allow-lan. The app blanks any external controller in a profile

Port is 1080 plus the Android user number. UDP goes through the SOCKS port unless a plugin is used without a UDP fallback profile; then TCP only. 'Share over LAN' binds 0.0.0.0. Last stable tag v5.3.4. Carries MasterDnsVPN through Mygod's SIP003 plugin (be.mygod.shadowsocks.plugin.masterdnsvpn, plugin id masterdnsvpn; v0.1.0 of 2026-08-29, APKs on GitHub only, built from MasterDnsVPN v2026.06.13.234407-7de2476): the MasterDnsVPN server forwards to one fixed Shadowsocks server. VPN mode with the plugin needs a build with PR #3227, first in v5.3.5-nightly (2026-02-10)

Docs list mixed ports 3067 (rules), 3066 (all proxy) and 3065 (all direct), SOCKS, HTTP and HTTPS on each; control (Clash API) 3057. The TUN switch is shown on every platform, but the Android service plugin and the core build are not public, so running without VpnService on Android is not verified. Core is a sing-box fork (KaringX/sing-box)

The Google Play build. Closed source, Xray core. Official docs mark the proxy and TUN mode parameters 'Desktop only'. They also list SOCKS and HTTP inbound authentication modes (socks-auth-mode: auto makes credentials and gives them to the tunnel) without saying which platforms; a loopback inbound in VPN mode is likely but its port is not documented

The GitHub build. Closed source, Xray core. Official docs mark the proxy and TUN mode parameters 'Desktop only'. They also list SOCKS and HTTP inbound authentication modes (socks-auth-mode: auto makes credentials and gives them to the tunnel) without saying which platforms; a loopback inbound in VPN mode is likely but its port is not documented

Version 8 (Aether core, Rust). The SOCKS port takes no password. HTTP is HTTP CONNECT on the SOCKS port plus one. 'Allow LAN access' binds 0.0.0.0. When Psiphon or Tor is chained inside WARP, Aether moves to 1829/1830 and the chained engine takes 1819. Versions 1 to 7 (warp-plus core) differ
VPN only in the public app code. The core (DXcore) is a private build, so whether it opens a loopback listener is unknown

v2rayNG fork with the Mahsa Xray core (also Psiphon); parts closed (README); public settings code is v2rayNG 1.8.5 era under com.MahsaNG.EMS; Psiphon mode has its own socks/http port fields (hints 20808/20809) and Allow LAN; Play developer Holistic Resilience. Not in apps.tsv
OpenVPN client. It can itself use a SOCKS or HTTP proxy, and it leaves Orbot out of its VPN on its own
No local proxy found in the Android source. WireGuard configs come from the website's configuration generator (paid account)
Shadowsocks access keys. The VPN's file descriptor goes straight to the in-process client; no loopback proxy. Only Outline itself is left out of the VPN
No local proxy found in the Android source. WireGuard configs only for paid accounts (Config Generator)

Beta build, not read separately; values from the stable source. Also a root mode. Tor's SOCKS on 9050 like Orbot; HTTPTunnel 8118 off by default. DNSCrypt (5354) and I2P (HTTP 4444, SOCKS 4447) run when enabled. In proxy mode, apps with their own proxy setting point at these ports

Also a root mode. Tor's SOCKS on 9050 like Orbot; HTTPTunnel 8118 off by default. DNSCrypt (5354) and I2P (HTTP 4444, SOCKS 4447) run when enabled. In proxy mode, apps with their own proxy setting point at these ports

Google Play build, not read separately; values from the stable source. Also a root mode. Tor's SOCKS on 9050 like Orbot; HTTPTunnel 8118 off by default. DNSCrypt (5354) and I2P (HTTP 4444, SOCKS 4447) run when enabled. In proxy mode, apps with their own proxy setting point at these ports
Imports .conf, zip and QR codes; exports every tunnel to Downloads/wireguard-export.zip after authentication unless exporting is disabled
The build from telegram.org. Messenger, not a VPN. It can itself use SOCKS5 or MTProto proxies; it opens no local proxy
The Google Play build. Messenger, not a VPN. It can itself use SOCKS5 or MTProto proxies; it opens no local proxy
Messenger, not a VPN. It can itself use SOCKS5 or MTProto proxies; it opens no local proxy
The audit app: no INTERNET permission. Watch is a separate package, org.visadahyu.datapavan.watch, and opens no port of its own
Successor of NekoBox. Port is 2080 plus the Android user number. 'Allow Connections from the LAN' binds 0.0.0.0. Not in apps.tsv yet
Archived on GitHub; last release 0.8.1-rc03 (2022). HTTP on 9080 off by default. Ports plus the Android user number. Not in apps.tsv

Closed source, HexaSoftware (hexasoftware.dev, which has only privacy and terms pages); no official channel found besides the store listings. Xray core (26.7.28 in 6.1.4) next to SSH, Hysteria2, Ping Tunnel, DNSTT and MasterDNS. MasterDnsVPN since Android 6.1.4 (Play 'What's new', listing updated 2026-09-21, archived copy of 2026-10-01; not in 6.1.2 of 2026-08-21); iOS V2Box and V2Box Pro since 10.1.8 (2026-09-15). 'Tunnel Mode (VPN/Proxy)' since Android 6.0.7 (2026-07-30); the Android proxy listener, port and auth are not documented. The iOS listing offers 'Share on Local SOCKS5 / HTTP (accessible over network)' with a custom port (iOS 10.0.8); an independent report (runetfreedom, April 2026) lists an unauthenticated loopback SOCKS5 open in VPN mode, port not given. V2Box Pro is iOS only (App Store id6756966178); HexaSoftware has no V2Box Pro package on Google Play. Not in apps.tsv

Closed source (Vonmatrix Co. Ltd; the channel says the build is DexProtector-obfuscated). Xray core (25.10.15 in January 2026); older builds also had Psiphon, which the 2026 listing no longer names. An independent report (runetfreedom, April 2026) lists an unauthenticated loopback SOCKS5 open in VPN mode, port not given. The official channel (2021-2022) said the app reports its SOCKS proxy details when the VPN starts and told users to point a hotspot client at them, so that old build served it beyond loopback. Per-app mode was dropped in 2022 for Play policy and is back in the 2026 listing

No public source (individual developer, Indonesia; also a Windows build). Xray core (v26.1.23 in September 2026) next to its own SSH, DNSTT ('SSH SlowDNS'), Hysteria2 and WireGuard clients. No official source shows MasterDnsVPN or slipstream as of 2026-11-11: the newest notes (Android 4.3.0.643; Play listing updated 2026-09-18, channel post of 2026-09-26) add only Hysteria2 and Xray 26.1.23. The proxy sharing feature is called Proxy Tethering (Android 4.2.0 notes, June 2026); the Windows notes say it serves SOCKS5 from a Tethering Manager. Its default state, address and port, and whether a loopback proxy runs in VPN mode, are not documented

Closed source. The official manual, undated and still naming Android 4.0, says its local HTTP proxy uses port 8989 (fixed), at 127.0.0.1, as the upstream for its own SSH and OpenVPN; also a root iptables mode. Whether 6.x builds keep it is unknown. Not in apps.tsv

Closed source. Cloudflare's docs say the local proxy mode (SOCKS5 or HTTPS) is on desktop clients only. Cloudflare offers no WireGuard export; unofficial registrars exist. Package has four 'one's. Not in apps.tsv

No public source, no docs. A one-tap free VPN on the developer's own servers, with ads; developer APNA SOFTWARE (SMC-PRIVATE) LIMITED, Karachi (Play account APNA TUNNEL). A third-party tutorial shows UDP, Super DNS, Fast DNS, DNS Lite and PDR modes. The iOS app 'AM TUNNEL LITE' is another seller's

Flutter app; transports dnstt (KCP and Noise, from a committed prebuilt gomobile dnstt.aar) and Slipstream (committed prebuilt slipstream-rust binary). The local port is not a SOCKS5 server: it pipes raw TCP into the tunnel, and the SOCKS5 is whatever the server forwards to; the app's connect check speaks SOCKS5 with no auth and a domain name, so a working setup has both. With the 'SSH' tunnel type the app runs its own SOCKS5 (CONNECT only, no auth, IPv6 refused) on a fixed 127.0.0.1:1080; Slipstream in VPN mode listens on a fixed 127.0.0.1:7000. VPN mode is its own packet loop: DNS goes to the chosen resolver outside the tunnel, other UDP is dropped, only an IPv4 route. Release builds use the debug signing config. GitHub releases only

Full flavour. Tunnel types DNSTT (default), NoizDNS, VayDNS, Soar, Slipstream, SSH, NaiveProxy, VLESS, Tor, DoH, and chains. The listener is a Kotlin SOCKS5 bridge: CONNECT and hev-socks5-tunnel's FWD_UDP (0x05, used for DNS) are taken, UDP ASSOCIATE gets 'command not supported', IPv6 CONNECT is refused. Behind it the DNS tunnel listens on the next port (127.0.0.1:10881), a raw pipe to the server's SOCKS5 (Dante, with the profile's credentials). First launch makes a random username and password but leaves auth off; code comments claim a random port and auth on. 'HTTP proxy' (8080) and 'Append HTTP Proxy to VPN' are off by default; listen address can be set to 0.0.0.0. GitHub and Telegram only; README disowns store copies

Lite flavour of the same source, without Tor and NaiveProxy. Tunnel types DNSTT (default), NoizDNS, VayDNS, Soar, Slipstream, SSH, NaiveProxy, VLESS, Tor, DoH, and chains. The listener is a Kotlin SOCKS5 bridge: CONNECT and hev-socks5-tunnel's FWD_UDP (0x05, used for DNS) are taken, UDP ASSOCIATE gets 'command not supported', IPv6 CONNECT is refused. Behind it the DNS tunnel listens on the next port (127.0.0.1:10881), a raw pipe to the server's SOCKS5 (Dante, with the profile's credentials). First launch makes a random username and password but leaves auth off; code comments claim a random port and auth on. 'HTTP proxy' (8080) and 'Append HTTP Proxy to VPN' are off by default; listen address can be set to 0.0.0.0. GitHub and Telegram only; README disowns store copies

Public source (Kotlin shell geph-android + gephgui UI + geph5-client engine run as libgeph.so; geph5-client is MPL-2.0). Same package on Play and the geph.io APK. No proxy-only mode on Android: the app always starts its VpnService. A switch, Local proxy (Settings > Local network), adds socks5:127.0.0.1:9909 and http:127.0.0.1:9910 while the VPN runs. It is off on fresh installs and on for installs older than the switch (2026-07). Listen on all interfaces binds 0.0.0.0 instead. Engine and proxy stop when the VPN is revoked, so they cannot outlive another VpnService. Per-app is exclude-only (Select excluded apps); Geph always excludes itself. SOCKS5 refuses IPv6 targets. Its local SOCKS5 takes no password, carries UDP and takes names

Closed source, OpenVPN Inc.; Play shows 3.7.2 (updated 2026-11-10), the release notes list 3.7.3. OpenVPN protocol only; imports .ovpn profiles (file or URL). Its Proxies menu is an HTTP proxy client for reaching the VPN server (host, port, optional username/password with basic auth), not a local listener. Split tunnelling is route-based (seamless split-tunneling); the official Android settings list has no app selection. Settings include Allow LAN Access and Seamless Tunnel; supports Always-on VPN

Closed source (no public source found); DATABRIDGES TECHNOLOGIES LTD; Xray core plus AmneziaWG core; a SOCKS5 authorization setting exists since 5.22.71 (default not documented); since 5.24.76 the tunnel is started by the Xray core; one package for phone and TV

Closed source (GitHub repo holds only README, docs and APKs); own native engine reading Surge-format profiles, no VLESS/Xray; local HTTP/SOCKS5 listeners come from profile keys http-listen and socks5-listen (no documented default); optional VPN HTTP proxy on Android 10+; Google Play page returns 404; no password parameter is documented for socks5-listen

Open source (AGPL-3.0) since 3.0.9 of 2026-09-29, github.com/CluvexStudio/ZedSecure, read at v3.1.8 (5551edad); developer Cluvex (t.me/CluvexStudio), Play publisher account UnboundTechCo. Xray and sing-box next to Psiphon, Tor, OpenConnect, IKEv2, SSH, WireGuard/AmneziaWG and the DNS tunnels DNSTT, VayDNS and MasterDNS (MasterDnsVPN). MasterDnsVPN on Android since the Play release the developer announced on 2026-09-18 (version not given; 3.0.7 followed on 2026-09-24); proxy-only mode for MasterDNS and the other non-Xray engines since 3.1.8 (2026-11-02), VPN only before. Those engines run behind an Xray front on the same port, which blocks UDP except DNS; the MasterDNS engine also listens on its own unauthenticated SOCKS5 at 127.0.0.1:10860-10869. In VPN mode the SOCKS port stays up but since 3.1.8 carries a random per-connection username and password by default ('Password on the local proxy'). HTTP on port+1 only with 'Add HTTP proxy to VPN' (off); LAN sharing on 0.0.0.0:10880 with a password (off). The Play build is signed with Google's key, the GitHub APKs with the developer's own. Not in apps.tsv

Vendored, slightly older copy of the upstream MasterDnsVPN Go core built with gomobile; the SOCKS5 server is the core's own (auth off, UDP ASSOCIATE relays only DNS to port 53, names passed to the server, SOCKS4/4a also accepted); default mode VPN (gVisor TUN bridge to the same listener); optional Internet Sharing (off by default) adds SOCKS5 0.0.0.0:8090 and HTTP 0.0.0.0:8091, open unless a user and password are both set; LISTEN_IP is an editable and importable profile field; active (HEAD 2026-11-05, last release v1.2.4 2026-05-18); GitHub releases only; listed by the upstream README. Not in apps.tsv

Vendored upstream MasterDnsVPN Go core built with gomobile (SOCKS5 code as upstream 4052a6b plus one added close); the SOCKS5 server is the core's own (auth off, UDP ASSOCIATE relays only DNS to port 53, names passed to the server); tunnel mode chosen per profile, default SOCKS5 (no VpnService), TUN mode bridges to the same listener; optional hotspot sharing (off by default) relays 0.0.0.0:8090 to the core's SOCKS5 and serves a PAC file on 0.0.0.0:8091; LISTEN_IP is an editable profile field; last commit and release v1.1.1 2026-09-23; GitHub releases with an in-app update check; listed by the upstream README. Not in apps.tsv

Modified vendored copy of the upstream MasterDnsVPN Go core plus tun2socks in one gomobile library; the SOCKS5 server is the core's own, forced to 127.0.0.1 on fixed port 18000 for the app's own tun2socks (no auth setting; tun2socks dials without credentials); UDP ASSOCIATE answers only DNS, by default resolved directly through Yandex DNS 77.88.8.8/77.88.8.1 outside the tunnel; IPv4 route only; no per-app choice; release v1.1 2026-09-15, 2 stars; GitHub releases only; not listed by the upstream README. Not in apps.tsv

Legacy Python MasterDnsVPN client, ported by hand and run through Chaquopy, with hev-socks5-tunnel for the TUN; the SOCKS5 server is that Python core's (127.0.0.1:1080 by default, LISTEN_IP must be 127.0.0.1, auth off, UDP ASSOCIATE relays only DNS to port 53); VPN only, full tunnel or an app allowlist; compatibility with current Go servers not documented; idle since release v1.0.9 2026-04-11; GitHub releases only; not listed by the upstream README. Not in apps.tsv

Default engine StormDNS, a fork of MasterDnsVPN release v2026.04.05.191930-7757d2d (CottenDNS and Lantern Soar selectable per profile); the SOCKS5 server is the engine's own (auth off, UDP ASSOCIATE relays only DNS to port 53, names passed to the server) and the HTTP proxy is the app's bridge; default mode Proxy, which also runs a local DNS listener on 127.0.0.1:10888; VPN mode (tun2proxy) forces 127.0.0.1:10886 with auth and HTTP off; source-available proprietary; active (release 1.6.16 2026-11-04); GitHub releases and Telegram t.me/whitedns, not on Play; not listed by the upstream README. Not in apps.tsv

SIP003 plugin for shadowsocks-android (plugin id masterdnsvpn) built from the upstream MasterDnsVPN core v2026.06.13.234407-7de2476 (pinned submodule plus a small embedding patch) in TCP-forward mode with the core's own SOCKS/TCP listener disabled; it listens only on the SS_LOCAL_HOST:SS_LOCAL_PORT the host app gives it, as a raw TCP forward to the Shadowsocks server; any local SOCKS5 belongs to shadowsocks-android; VPN mode needs a shadowsocks-android build with PR #3227 (v5.3.5-nightly or later); one commit, release v0.1.0 2026-08-29; Apache-2.0; GitHub releases only; not listed by the upstream README. Not in apps.tsv
